{{Short description|English chemist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Sir Hugh Fish''', [[CBE]] (6 January 1923 – 27 May 1999) was an English chemist who was one of the architects of the UK [[water industry]] in the late 20th century, and was responsible for the clean-up of the [[River Thames]].<ref name=Indy>[https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/obituaries-sir-hugh-fish-1099543.html ''The Independent'' 11 June 1999] "Obituaries: Sir Hugh Fish"</ref><ref name=nytimes>[https://www.nytimes.com/1999/07/21/world/hugh-fish-76-who-made-thames-so-clean-the-salmon-came-back.html ''New York Times''  21 July 1999] "Hugh Fish, 76, Who Made Thames So Clean the Salmon Came Back"</ref>

==Life==
Fish was born in [[Woodlesford]], [[West Yorkshire]] on 6 January 1923, and went to [[The Rodillian Academy|Rothwell Grammar School]].  He then studied [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Leeds]], but broke off to join the [[Royal Naval Volunteer Reserve]] in 1942, serving on the [[Arctic convoys of World War II]] and rising to the rank of lieutenant by the end of the war.  He completed his degree and began his professional life as a chemist.<ref name=Indy/><ref name=nytimes/>
He married Nancy Asquith (died 4 October 2005<ref name=Times>''The Times'' 6 Oct 2005</ref>) in 1943 and they had two sons and a daughter. He died in [[Wallingford, Oxfordshire]] on 27 May 1999.<ref name=Indy/>

==Career==
He held scientific posts related to rivers and rose to become chief executive of [[Thames Water Authority]] from 1978 to 1984.  During this period the water quality improved so that over 100 species of fish were present,<ref name=Indy/> and a [[salmon]] was caught in 1985.<ref name=nytimes/> In 1976 he was appointed to the board of the [[Natural Environment Research Council]] and was chairman for four years from 1984.  He was then involved in overseeing the [[privatisation]] of the water industry as a member of the board of the [[National Rivers Authority]].<ref name=Indy/>

==Honours==
He received an OBE in 1971 and  CBE in 1984.  He was knighted in 1989.  He served as President of the [[Institute of Fisheries Management]] and was a Visiting Professor of the [[University of Hertfordshire]]. He was a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] and of the Institute of Water and Environmental Management.<ref name=Indy/>
